clue.text: Bishop puts on jumper and twitches showing street dance style

indicators.note: to put on clothing is to wear it, so the garment goes around whoever wears it

parts.note: a kangaroo, the classic jumper
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
tics are involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: A clergyman pulls on a sweater and starts jerking about like a breakdancer.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper in Britain is a sweater, which is the picture, but here it is the kangaroo that the bishop is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotics, also called the robot, is a hip-hop dance imitating a machine's jerky mechanical movements.

clue.text: Set aside article carried by upset outcast

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting something turns it on its head, so the letters read bottom to top
whatever is carried is held inside its carrier

parts.note: a leper is a social outcast
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item is pushed aside by an angry pariah.
explanation.walkthrough: The outcast is turned over first, then the article is slipped inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or annul it, just as a court sets aside a ruling.

clue.text: Cork sound in top of bottle diverging from the norm

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the opening letter of a word

parts.note: its opening letter
a rogue element departs from what is normal

explanation.surface: A wine buff notes an odd noise as the cork leaves a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork is not a stopper but the Irish city and county, so its 'sound' is the way people there speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially an Irish one, the speech heard in Cork.

clue.text: Flower found in the middle of unctuous sauce

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its central pair of letters when the length is even

parts.note: the two central letters of an eight-letter word
sauce and lip both mean cheeky impudence

explanation.surface: A bloom turns up in a greasy gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce is cheek, insolence, not something poured; British slang uses lip for the same backchat.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring-blooming bulb plant with cup-shaped petals, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Scope of Commissioner's licence

parts.note: COM is a standard abbreviation for commissioner
a pass is a permit allowing entry or action

explanation.surface: It describes the extent of an official's permit or authority.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about an official's powers, but it splits after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass can mean range or extent, as in 'within the compass of the inquiry'.

clue.text: Find innocent Parisian who gets caught in act

indicators.note: something caught in a trap sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A French suspect caught red-handed is nonetheless cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals that the next word is translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquitting a defendant is the court formally declaring them not guilty of the charge.

clue.text: Conservative member's miserable retreat

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
an arm or leg is a member of the body
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's humiliating policy U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a Member of Parliament, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb-down is a humiliating withdrawal from a stated position, an embarrassing backing off.

clue.text: Volcanic material rises after mounted man causes disturbance

parts.note: a mounted rider is up on the horse
the male pronoun

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: molten rock from a volcano

explanation.surface: Lava welling up beside a horseman throws everything into turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the overturned volcanic material at the end, behind the mounted man.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a violent or sudden disruption, a great disorder or commotion.

clue.text: Chance to get on top of business

parts.note: your turn is your chance or go
over means above

explanation.surface: An opportunity to get on top of one's work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the chance sits above the word for 'on top of', so the order follows the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's turnover is the volume of trade it does, the amount of sales in a period.

clue.text: Almost detect unpleasant aroma returning after publicist exposes difficulties

indicators.note: almost all means one short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the publicist's trade

indicators.note: going back the way it came, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: smell, meaning to sense, missing its last letter
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A PR person's nose sniffs out trouble and lays it bare.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the shortened sense and the body odour turn round together and follow the publicist.
explanation.definitionFit: Problems and difficulties are straightforward synonyms for troubles needing to be overcome.

clue.text: Pitcher, taking time, flustered non-entity

indicators.note: someone flustered is in a state of confusion, so the letters are muddled
taking something away removes it

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A baseball pitcher takes too long and goes to pieces as a nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' here means taking away, not including; the remaining letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher can mean a person of no importance, literally a zero, someone who counts for nothing.

clue.text: Topple yew over concealing bark

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters go back to front
the words keep something tucked out of sight within them

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Fell a yew tree and hide the bark under it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bark looks like the tree's outer layer, matching yew, but it is the dog's noise; the answer runs backwards across the end of 'Topple' and 'yew'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelp is a short sharp cry, much like a dog's bark.

clue.text: Pale blue jet to glide on water?

parts.note: aqua is a light greenish-blue
a jet is an aeroplane

explanation.surface: A light-blue aircraft sets down on a lake, gliding across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the playful, slightly loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To aquaplane is to skim over a wet surface on a film of water, like a car losing grip.

clue.text: British eggs — flipping good for you!

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for British

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round

parts.note: ova are egg cells

explanation.surface: A cheery British advert insisting eggs are flipping good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British intensifier, as in 'flipping marvellous', but it turns the eggs round.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is an exclamation of praise and approval, a congratulatory cheer for an achievement.

clue.text: Coffee shop's hidden charges

indicators.note: concealed within, so the letters sit inside the words before it

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A café sneaks extra costs onto the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of the first word and the start of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Fees are payments demanded for a service, which is what charges are.

clue.text: European statement about Roman numerals impacts church life

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
the true statement 'X is ten' about a numeral
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A European pronouncement about Latin numbering shakes up church life.
explanation.walkthrough: The statement is a sentence one might say about Roman numerals: the letter X stands for ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence and life both mean being alive or the state of being, as in 'a miserable existence'.

clue.text: Lying about Greg Dyke's body is obscene

indicators.note: around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: lying face down
Greg Dyke chaired the Football Association, English football's governing body

explanation.surface: Telling lies about a former BBC boss's physique would be indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: Dyke's 'body' is not his physique but the organisation he chaired, the FA.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane language is irreverent or vulgar, close in sense to obscene or blasphemous talk.

clue.text: Parasite contaminated mop water

indicators.note: something contaminated has been fouled and spoilt, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dirty floor-mopping water harbours a parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: The dirty water is just the letter supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapeworm is a flat segmented worm living in the gut, a classic example of a parasite.

clue.text: Warning: Drama portrays scenes of a sexual nature

parts.note: the golfer's shout warning of an incoming ball
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A TV content warning: this drama contains sexual scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes it look like a broadcaster's caution, but the warning is the golfer's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreplay is the erotic stimulation preceding intercourse, so the activity in such scenes, loosely defined.

clue.text: Group with trouble worshipping

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
a ring is a gang or circle of people

explanation.surface: A congregation having difficulties during prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply puts the two pieces side by side, the trouble first.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring and worshipping both describe revering someone with intense love and devotion.

clue.text: Pull back before beginning to fall into abyss

indicators.note: going back means the letters read the other way

parts.note: to lug is to drag or haul

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone stops short just before toppling over a precipice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull back' is not recoiling: the word for pull is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulf is a deep chasm or wide gap, exactly as an abyss is.

clue.text: Curse Juliet with kiss containing one last bit of poison

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its closing letter

parts.note: its closing letter
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Romeo and Juliet's fatal ending: a kiss with poison on his lips.
explanation.walkthrough: The kiss holds the numeral and the poison's last letter; it follows the J.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx is a spell bringing bad luck, so it serves as a hex or curse.

clue.text: Lift lid up revealing big prize

parts.note: to jack up is to raise

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: a lid is a top

explanation.surface: Raise the lid of the box and see the grand prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift lid up' reads as one action; the first word is the lifting piece and 'up' flips the lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the largest prize in a lottery or game, the top payout.

clue.text: Champagne the French prove a failure

parts.note: fizz is informal for champagne
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French champagne turns out to be a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' means the French word for 'the', not the people.
explanation.definitionFit: To fizzle, or fizzle out, is to end feebly after a promising start, so to flop.

clue.text: Nepali phrase misread

indicators.note: read wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Nepalese saying gets misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nepali' looks like an adjective for the phrase but is a noun, a person from Nepal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherpas are a people of the Nepalese Himalaya, famed as mountain guides, so one is an example.

clue.text: Dismiss leaders of empanelled jury ending criminal trial

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so each word yields its opening letter

parts.note: opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A judge sends the jury away as a criminal trial ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending' looks like a selection signal but is just one of the words supplying an initial.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone is to throw them out or expel them, close to dismissing them.

clue.text: Key worker dreads that man coming back around end of August

parts.note: dreadlocks, shortened to dreads

indicators.note: returning, so the letters run backwards
surrounding, so one piece is put about another

parts.note: the male pronoun

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter

parts.note: its closing letter

explanation.surface: An essential worker fears that someone will return in late August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' evokes the pandemic phrase for essential staff, but it is someone who works with keys. 'Dreads' is not a verb but dreadlocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith makes and repairs locks and cuts keys, literally a tradesman whose job is keys.

clue.text: Pierce head of saltwater fish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: its opening letter
the pike is a predatory fish

explanation.surface: Spearing the head of a sea fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The pike is a freshwater fish, so 'saltwater fish' cannot be read as one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To spike something is to impale it on a sharp point, which is to pierce it.

clue.text: Shape of longbow almost entirely bent

indicators.note: nearly all of it, so the final letter goes
bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted round

parts.note: the weapon minus its last letter

explanation.surface: An archer notices the curve of a well-flexed longbow.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawn bow is bent, so 'bent' sits naturally in the surface while signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle longer than it is wide, an example of a geometric figure.

clue.text: Goblin squeezes Beelzebub's heart getting drop of red to drink

indicators.note: squeezing holds something tightly in a grip

parts.note: a sprite is a mischievous elf

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A devilish imp grips Satan and is given some red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Beelzebub is a name for the Devil; his heart is just the middle letter. The red drop goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is wine, often white, mixed with soda water, an example of a long drink.

clue.text: Home secretary confronts border chaos

parts.note: Theresa May was Britain's Home Secretary from 2010 to 2016
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A government minister faces disorder on the national frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Secretary is the British minister for policing and immigration; this one is named, not described. 'Border' is a sewing edge, not a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder and confusion, a direct synonym for utter chaos.

clue.text: Pace setter misses two starts misbehaving and so forth

indicators.note: missing the opening letters means each word loses its first
behaving badly, out of order, so the letters go astray

parts.note: each word without its opening letter

explanation.surface: A race pacemaker fluffs two starts and generally misbehaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'two starts' are the opening letters of both words, not two false starts in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin meaning 'and the rest', used to show a list continues similarly.
